SOURCE-ASPECT NOTE: measured source is landscape (1600x679); this describes the reference, not the output canvas. Recompose its subjects, silhouettes, object relationships, light, surface and framing grammar on a landscape canvas. Keep subject proportions and source identity; no stretching, cropping, or padding to force orientation, no pasted source panel or unrelated replacement scene.
Require at least one structural change to arrangement, grouping/object count, or spatial logic; scale shifts, cropping and surface distress alone do not count. Keep distinctive source silhouettes, motifs, light and material relationships recognizable in the new structure.
TRANSFORM
Gilt reliquary crash world: off-center aperture with floating counterweight, frontal flat plate. One oversized Gothic gilt triple arch, pinnacles cropped at the top edge, sits left of center; through its openings, glowing vermilion and acid-green candlestick strokes fall across tarred wrinkled canvas, ending in a small green rebound. Right, a black fuzzy soot-ball with two glossy eyes and pale grin hovers in dot-speckled plaster space. Black-white chevron floor tilts upward into the wall. Flat museum light, gold glints, no lettering.
COMPOSITION
Do not start by duplicating the original source framing and object layout. Start from the strongest borrowed source elements, then recompose them through off-center aperture with a floating counterweight / frontal flat plate with pinnacles cropped at the top edge and the tilted chevron floor entering from the bottom. candlestick cascade falling through the gilt arch openings; soot-ball eclipse isolated in speckled negative space.
ANCHORS
Compose exactly 1 distinct source-native physical feature within the artwork: Oversized Gothic gilt triple arch framing the falling candlestick strokes. Keep it large and visibly separable; never a counted symbol, card, pasted thumbnail or UI label. No painted indicators. No visible annotation glyphs or QA chrome. No registration targets, crosshairs, reticles or hollow target rings.
LIMITS
Flat even museum light with sharp gold glints on the tracery and a faint neon bloom bleeding from the red and green strokes; materials: burnished gilt tracery; tarred wrinkled canvas; spray-glow pigment strokes; dot-speckled plaster; palette: tar black and bone beige grounds lit by gold, vermilion, and acid green.
